claims.value: The prior durable architecture replaced the monolithic mega-base with an Update 1-only distributed backbone-and-spurs network: a protected core hub, modular low-heat cells, mining spurs/outposts, and rail upgrades only when measured throughput requires them.

The new requirement is one Constructorizer and two Facturers while every Base Core remains level 0. Their heavy-machine heat is 500 + (2 × 650) = 1,800. A level-0 core has 1,000 capacity, and exceeding it disables Fire Wave protection. Every co-location is unsafe: Constructorizer + Facturer = 1,150; two Facturers = 1,300; all three = 1,800.

The safe revised layout uses three occupied level-0 cores: Core A hosts only the 500-heat Constructorizer as its heavy machine, leaving 500 capacity; Cores B and C each host only one 650-heat Facturer as their heavy machine, leaving 350 capacity apiece. All local processors, generators, storage, and logistics must fit inside those respective remaining margins; no heavy-machine pair may share a core.

Before construction, verify the live Update 1 build menu, recipes, unlocks, and existing load at each intended core; then produce a per-core bill of materials proving total heat does not exceed 1,000 and preferably retains operating margin. Use no hidden, future, or pre-Update-1 equipment, and do not rely on disputed Base Core Amplifier capacity until verified in-game.

claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer. It preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state—including evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved questions, rejected paths, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, advance, and hand off complex work. Obsidian and Markdown remain prototype inputs, projections, and export formats rather than the canonical product boundary.

The historical token result—about 1,070 mean estimated tokens for one-shot BM25 top-k versus 2,932 for the stateful workspace—belongs to the narrow retrieval-readiness benchmark; it does not establish that cached replay is uncached per-case input or that BM25 is the target architecture. Under the new gate, cumulative cached replay and uncached input must be measured and reported separately. Retrieval policy 0.2 and the process-per-operation BM25 shell remain regression fixtures only.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned workspace implementing one end-to-end N→N+1 transition: reopen parent checkpoint cp_de0046ff6008f7e71798 at rev_000001_5bb8d7cf1222; refresh to rev_000002_7323ec9a8a69 and return the changed evidence or constraint as a diff; provide exact and lexical retrieval plus a pluggable semantic path; batch query and read through a typed API; and atomically persist an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent ID and source references without reconstructing the unchanged corpus.

The implementation advances only when the transition harness completes each case in no more than four workspace calls, reproduces the claims produced by direct-filesystem access, exposes the N→N+1 diff, persists an immutable source-preserving child linked to its parent, avoids complete prior-corpus reconstruction when checkpoint plus delta suffice, and reports cumulative cached replay separately from uncached input.
